outcomes.original: Filing step: Register for a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate and obtain a California Seller's Permit. What to say: Register online with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector within 30 days of starting business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, etc.). The registration year runs April 1 to March 31. Apply for a California Seller's Permit (free) at the CDTFA online portal; it is required before ABC will process a license application. Every other city department asks for your Business Account Number, so complete this step before filing with Planning or DPH.

What to say: Submit the CUA application online (forms at sfplanning.org) with the project narrative, floor plans showing the merged bar area, a good-neighbor policy, operating hours (state 6 a.m.–2 a.m. to stay within principally-permitted hours), soundproofing measures (acoustic report or commitment to install soundproofing so bass and noise are not audible beyond the premises), a sidewalk-maintenance and litter-control plan (daily monitoring within one block), and a community-outreach summary. outcomes.original: Filing step: Coordinate the ABC license application or transfer in parallel with the CUA filing. What to say: If the concept serves full liquor, engage an ABC license broker before signing the lease to locate and escrow a Type 47 or Type 48 license. If the concept serves only beer and wine, apply for a new Type 41 or Type 42 through ABC's online portal, submitting the signed lease, entity documents, seller's permit, and a 30-day public posting notice at the premises. ABC will refer the application to SFPD and Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will not sign off until the CUA is approved, so time the ABC filing to land after the CUA hearing date is set. Expect 60–150 days for ABC processing, with an additional 1–3 months if the census tract requires a Public Convenience or Necessity finding due to undue concentration (which the density flag suggests is likely).
outcomes.note: The record shows undue concentration flag exists but does not state the license types, filing procedures, timelines, or agency requirements described in the sentence.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: The day and cost ranges are for the Conditional Use Authorization and Health permit to operate (the two approvals in the entitlement path) when they are granted. The CUA filing to hearing takes 120–300 days (catalog entry verified; comparables show 8–353 days for seven approved CUA cases, with the Castro Theatre CUA taking 353 days from filing to approval in June 2023). The health permit takes 14–45 days after plan check and final inspection. The CUA fee for a no-construction project is approximately $3,100 (CPI-adjusted from the 2023–24 schedule); larger projects or projects with construction pay higher fees up to $15,000. The health plan check is $828–$2,500 and the permit to operate application is $470 (FY2026–27 verified rates). ABC license costs are not included because the alcohol row status is insufficient information: a new Type 41 or 42 is $1,000–$1,600 and takes 60–150 days; a transferred Type 47 or 48 costs $100,000–$450,000 for the license itself plus $1,000–$1,600 in ABC fees and takes 90–240 days including escrow. Building permit fees ($800–$15,000) and time (14–120 days) are also excluded because that row's status is insufficient information pending occupancy-group confirmation. Notes: The day and cost ranges are for the Conditional Use Authorization and Health permit to operate (the two approvals in the entitlement path) when they are granted. The CUA filing to hearing takes 120–300 days (catalog entry verified). The Castro Theatre CUA taking 353 days from filing to approval in June 2023. The health permit takes 14–45 days after plan check and final inspection. The CUA fee for a no-construction project is approximately $3,100 (CPI-adjusted from the 2023–24 schedule); larger projects or projects with construction pay higher fees up to $15,000. The health plan check is $828–$2,500 and the permit to operate application is $470 (FY2026–27 verified rates). ABC license costs are not included because the alcohol row status is insufficient information: a new Type 41 or 42 is $1,000–$1,600 and takes 60–150 days; a transferred Type 47 or 48 costs $100,000–$450,000 for the license itself plus $1,000–$1,600 in ABC fees and takes 90–240 days including escrow. Building permit fees ($800–$15,000) and time (14–120 days) are also excluded because that row's status is insufficient information pending occupancy-group confirmation. These figures assume approval; they are not times or costs to a denial or withdrawal.
